name: Density Functional Theory and VASP
homeTitle: DFT and VASP Course: Density Functional Theory from Scratch
tagline: An interactive course from the Schrödinger equation to calculations you can defend.
description: A free, interactive course on density functional theory and VASP: quantum mechanics, Kohn–Sham DFT, k-points, plane waves, PAW, and calculations you can defend.

author.name: Osman Goni Ridwan
author.affiliation: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
author.bio: I'm a computational materials scientist and Ph.D. candidate in Mechanical Engineering at the University of North Carolina at Charlotte, and an Academic Cooperation Participant at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. I use DFT and VASP in my research on rare-earth permanent magnets, proton-conducting ceramics, carbon allotropes and molecular crystals, alongside machine-learning interatomic potentials and generative models.

parts.title: Quantum mechanics you need
parts.milestone: Explain why electronic structure is a many-body problem, and what “self-consistent” means.

parts.title: Density functional theory
parts.milestone: Explain the chain from the Schrödinger equation through Born–Oppenheimer, the many-electron problem, the density, Hohenberg–Kohn and Kohn–Sham to the exchange–correlation energy and the SCF loop.

parts.title: How VASP represents electrons
parts.milestone: Explain why VASP uses periodic cells, k-points, plane waves, ENCUT, PAW datasets and the POTCAR.

parts.title: Beyond semilocal functionals
parts.milestone: Compare PBE, DFT+U, r²SCAN, dispersion-corrected DFT and HSE by approximation, cost and typical failures.

parts.title: From energies and forces to materials properties
Doing DFT responsibly
parts.milestone: Design, critique and defend a DFT methodology for a real research problem.

lectures.title: Introduction to density functional theory
lectures.question: What does a DFT calculation compute, and what does VASP do when you press run?
lectures.description: What density functional theory computes, why it works with the electron density, where its one approximation sits, and what VASP does when you run it.
outcomes: what a DFT calculation takes in and what it gives back
why DFT works with the electron density instead of the many-electron wavefunction
where DFT's one approximation sits, and the errors it is known for
what VASP does with its four input files, from the first SCF step to the outputs
how to convert between the energy units of theory papers and of VASP

lectures.title: The Born–Oppenheimer approximation
lectures.question: What physical problem is VASP solving when it relaxes a structure?
lectures.description: What VASP actually solves: the electron–nuclear Hamiltonian, the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, potential-energy surfaces, forces and structural relaxation.
outcomes: which particles and interactions the full Hamiltonian of a material contains
why the nuclei can be clamped while the electrons are solved, and what that neglects
how an energy surface gives forces, and why a relaxation solves the electrons again at every step
which physical approximations a VASP relaxation makes before any functional is chosen

lectures.title: Wavefunctions, operators and eigenvalues
lectures.question: What does Ĥψ = Eψ actually mean?
lectures.description: Wavefunctions, operators and eigenvalues, worked through a particle in a box: probability, measurement, Hermitian operators, Hc = Ec and VASP's band energies.
outcomes: what a wavefunction is, and how |ψ|² gives probabilities
what operators, eigenfunctions and eigenvalues are
what a measurement returns, and how an expectation value differs from an eigenvalue
how a basis turns Ĥψ = Eψ into a matrix problem, Hc = Ec
what NBANDS and VASP's eigenvalues are, and why they are not, in general, measured energies

lectures.title: The variational principle and basis sets
lectures.question: How does an unsolvable differential equation become a finite calculation?
lectures.description: The variational principle and basis sets: why trial energies are upper bounds, how Hc = ESc arises, why bigger bases converge, and what VASP's ENCUT controls.
outcomes: why the energy of any trial wavefunction is an upper bound to the ground-state energy
how a basis expansion turns the problem into Hc = ESc
why a larger nested basis can only lower the energy, and what it costs
how ENCUT sets the size of VASP's plane-wave basis
why numerical convergence is different from physical accuracy

lectures.title: Atomic orbitals, core and valence electrons
lectures.seo: Atomic Orbitals, Core and Valence Electrons
lectures.question: Where do s, p, d and f, and “core” versus “valence”, come from?
lectures.description: Atomic orbitals from hydrogen to titanium: quantum numbers, nodes, shielding, filling order, and how core, semicore and valence electrons decide your POTCAR.
outcomes: what n, ℓ and m label, and how they set an orbital's shape and nodes
why many-electron atoms fill their orbitals in the order they do, with exceptions such as Cr and Cu
what distinguishes core, semicore and valence electrons
what changes in a calculation when you choose Ti, Ti_pv or Ti_sv

lectures.title: Pauli exclusion and Slater determinants
lectures.question: What makes many electrons harder than one, and what does the Pauli principle demand?
lectures.description: Electron spin, the Pauli exclusion principle and Slater determinants: antisymmetry, the exchange hole, what one determinant misses, and why codes never store Ψ.
outcomes: why electron–electron repulsion makes the many-electron problem hard
what spin is, and what a spin-orbital is
why electron wavefunctions are antisymmetric, and how a Slater determinant builds that in
how antisymmetry gives the Pauli exclusion principle and the exchange hole
why codes store one-electron orbitals and the density instead of the many-electron wavefunction

lectures.title: The Hartree–Fock method
lectures.question: What is the best you can do with one Slater determinant, and what does it miss?
lectures.description: The Hartree–Fock method from scratch: exchange, the Fock operator, self-interaction, the SCF loop, Koopmans' theorem and correlation, with helium solved live.
outcomes: where the exchange term comes from, and what the Fock operator contains
why exchange cancels the self-interaction that a Hartree mean field contains
how the Hartree–Fock equations become a matrix problem that must be solved self-consistently
what orbital energies mean: Koopmans' theorem, and why their sum is not the total energy
what the correlation energy is, and how Hartree–Fock relates to Kohn–Sham DFT
